svg.title: The table and the bread of the Presence, Exodus 25:23-30
svg.desc: Plate in four parts. The table of Exodus 25 in side elevation, drawn to scale at two cubits long and one and a half high: acacia overlaid with gold, a gold molding around the top, a rim a handbreadth wide drawn dashed between the legs because its place is not given, a ring at each leg holding a pole, and twelve loaves on it in two stacks of six with frankincense on each, the stacks and the frankincense dishes dashed because the arrangement is the Mishnah's reading and no dish is named. Beside it, what the text states and what it leaves unstated. Below, the twelve loaves drawn both ways the Hebrew allows, two rows of six and two stacks of six, both dashed; the week of the bread, set out every Sabbath, kept before the LORD, then eaten by the priests in a holy place as hot bread replaces it; and a strip following the table from the tabernacle through the wilderness, David at Nob, Solomon's ten tables, Malachi and Ezekiel, to Jesus' words about David and the bread, the table of the Lord, and Jesus' promise of His table in His kingdom.
svg.text: The Table and the Bread of the Presence
“You shall set the bread of the Presence on the table before me regularly” (Exodus 25:30, ESV)
What Moses was told to make
rim, a handbreadth: place not given
ring at a leg, pole through it
Drawn to scale from Exodus 25:23. The loaves’
arrangement, the rim’s place and the poles are
not stated: dashed, or a tradition named

Twelve loaves, in two sets of six
the Hebrew allows both; stacks: Mishnah
Whether the rim stood above the top
Length of the poles, shape of the
Leviticus 24:6: “two מַעֲרָכוֹת, six in each.” The word means an
arrangement set in order: ESV “piles,” WEB “rows.”
The Mishnah (Menachot 11:5-6) has two stacks held apart by gold
supports and hollow reeds, each loaf ten handbreadths long with
its ends turned up. That is the tradition of the Second Temple;
Exodus and Leviticus say only “six in each.”
eaten by the priests in a holy place
hot bread put in its place
Where the table stands in Scripture
Dashed: seen in a vision (Ezekiel), or promised and still to come (Luke 22:30).
